questions.question: If hazards are on your left, where should you ride?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
In any portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the right portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride in the right portion of the lane. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: What makes night riding safer?

options.text: Night riding is not safe because other drivers cannot see your turn signals.
It should only be done in the city.

questions.explanation: Wear reflective clothing when riding at night. This helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: What color is a warning sign with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What is the correct body position on a motorcycle?

options.text: Sit forward enough that your arms are slightly bent when holding the grips.
Sit as far back as possible and stretch to reach the grips.
Lean over the bike so your arms hold you up.
Keep your knees far from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit forward enough that your arms are slightly bent when holding the grips.
questions.explanation: Sit forward so your arms are slightly bent at the grips. This helps you reach and operate the controls easily and comfortably.

questions.question: What happens when you take a turn too fast?

options.text: It is fine as long as you stay under the speed limit.
It is safer on a motorcycle than in a car.
It is fine as long as no other vehicles are near you.
You may end up in another lane or leave the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may end up in another lane or leave the road.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast is dangerous. You may not hold the turn and could end up in another lane or off the road. Be careful when turning.

questions.question: The body eliminates about one drink per hour. If someone drank 8 drinks 4 hours ago, how many drinks are likely still in their body?
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. After 4 hours, about 4 drinks remain in the system.

questions.question: What is downshifting also called?
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows the motorcycle like braking. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: How many brakes do most motorcycles have?

options.text: A front brake and a rear brake.
Three brakes: front, rear, and emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: A front brake and a rear brake.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes: one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: How can you reduce your risk of an accident?

options.text: Try to blend into traffic so other drivers don't notice you.
Don't use turn signals unless riding at night.
Use turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
Ride close to the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
questions.explanation: Reduce crash risk by being visible. Use your turn signals, brake light, and proper lane position to tell other drivers what you are doing. Keep safe distance from others, look ahead 12 seconds, and be ready for hazards.

questions.question: Which is not protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Riders should wear a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves for protection.

questions.question: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like cars. When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Slow down so any vehicle in your blind spot can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for vehicles before changing lanes.

questions.question: What does reflective material on your helmet do?

options.text: Makes you more visible to other drivers.
Should only be used at night.
Does not help you be seen.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes you more visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: Reflective material on a vest or helmet makes you more visible to other drivers. Use it both day and night.

questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Do a thorough inspection before every ride. Small problems on a motorcycle can be more dangerous than on a car.

questions.question: How can you help other drivers see you on your motorcycle?

options.text: Do not use your turn signals.

questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright colors, use your headlight at all times, and use your turn signals.

questions.question: What is the correct way to check your tire pressure?

options.text: Look at the tire and guess.
Compare the tire height to another tire.

questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check tire pressure before every ride. Under-inflated tires may look fine, so looking alone is not enough.

questions.question: What material should you look for in a protective jacket or pants?
questions.explanation: Wear long pants and a jacket to protect your arms and legs. Leather clothing offers the best protection.

questions.question: How can over-the-counter drugs like cold tablets affect your riding?

options.text: They can reduce your ability to ride safely.
They usually do not affect your ability to ride safely.
They pose no risk to your riding ability.
They are always safe to take before riding because they are sold over-the-counter.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can reduce your ability to ride safely.
questions.explanation: Most drugs, including over-the-counter medications, can affect your ability to ride safely. Check the side effects of any drug before riding.

questions.question: What should your helmet meet to provide the best protection?
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state safety standards. It should fit snugly and have no visible defects.

questions.question: What is your best source of information about your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Use your owner's manual as your main source for information about your specific motorcycle. It includes specifications, operation, and maintenance instructions.

questions.question: Most crashes happen in daylight. How can you be more visible?
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen in daylight. Always wear bright colors while riding, even during the day.

questions.question: How can you reduce your chances of having an accident?

options.text: Ride one foot behind the vehicle in front of you.
Signal only when you want to.
Stay alert and be ready to avoid a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay alert and be ready to avoid a crash.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, stay visible to other drivers. Use your signals, brake lights, and lane position to show what you are doing. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: When you adjust your rearview mirror, make sure you can see:

options.text: The lane behind you and the lane next to you.
Only the lane next to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane behind you and the lane next to you.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much as possible of the lane beside you. A properly adjusted mirror may show part of your arm or shoulder, but the road behind and beside you is most important.

questions.question: How do you control the accelerator on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The accelerator on a motorcycle is on the right handgrip. You control it with your right hand.

questions.question: A motorcycle rider can slow down by:
questions.explanation: Downshifting is a way to slow down your motorcycle. Know that downshifting does not turn on the brake lights.

questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. It only takes a few minutes and helps prevent problems before you ride.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a good clothing choice for riding?

options.text: A jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs
Boots or shoes that cover your ankles
A baseball cap to cover your hair

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap to cover your hair
questions.explanation: To protect yourself from injury, wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high boots or shoes that support your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: Your body can only get rid of alcohol through:
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to remove alcohol. There are no quick ways to sober up.

questions.question: Shifting to a lower gear has the same effect as:
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows your motorcycle down, similar to using the brakes. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: What should you check during a pre-ride inspection?

options.text: The wear and tread of your tires

questions.correctAnswerText: The wear and tread of your tires
questions.explanation: Before every ride, inspect your tires, oil and fluid levels, headlight, tail light, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol, you should:

options.text: Decide if you can ride based on how you feel after drinking.
Set a drinking limit so you can still ride safely.
Not worry about riding if you feel fine.

questions.explanation: The safest choice is to not ride after drinking any alcohol. Even small amounts of alcohol can affect your ability to ride safely.
